column1:
- Macro policy stance: The FOMC held the federal funds rate at 2.25–2.50% and emphasized patience, looking through transitory energy-driven disinflation while core inflation hovers near 2%. Labor markets remain strong even as spending and capex have slowed.
- Inflation expectations: Market-based compensation remains low and survey-based measures are little changed, supporting a cautious approach rather than preemptive tightening.
- Implementation: IOER/ON RRP operations keep the funds rate in range; continued Treasury/MBS reinvestment caps maintain balance sheet normalization.
- FSR overlay: The Financial Stability Report highlights vulnerabilities from elevated asset valuations in some markets and high corporate leverage, even as bank capital/liquidity are strong and short-term funding risks remain low. These stability considerations reinforce a watchful, patient stance despite solid employment conditions.
- Net assessment: Balanced but dovish-leaning, tempered by noted financial vulnerabilities; supportive of sustained expansion while guarding against downside inflation and stability risks.
